content: Indication-specific dosing for L-lysine and lysine monohydrochloride (lysine) includes the following regimens: For oral administration: 1000 mg taken by mouth once daily to three times daily for a duration of 6 to 12 months. For topical application: Super Lysine Plus is applied every 2 hours for 11 days. For oral administration in divided doses: 10 g taken by mouth daily, divided into multiple doses, for up to 5 days. These dosing regimens are used for purposes such as athletic performance enhancement, treatment of herpes simplex labialis, and management of metabolic alkalosis. L-lysine is possibly effective for the treatment of herpes simplex labialis. Reported adverse effects include diarrhea and abdominal pain. Chronic renal failure and interstitial nephritis have also been noted. No significant drug interactions have been reported. L-lysine is contraindicated in individuals with kidney disease. During pregnancy, L-lysine falls under the category of avoid use, as its safety has not been established. Similarly, its use during lactation is also advised against. Pregnancy Category A indicates that controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk, but this does not apply to L-lysine, as its use is not recommended during pregnancy or lactation.
